title: The Lord of the Rings, Tolkien
subject: litterature
description: Frodo must destroy the One Ring at Mount Doom. Tolkien invents Middle-earth and redefines modern fantasy.

hero.hook: One ring to rule them all: the epic that invented fantasy as we know it.

blocks.text: **The Lord of the Rings**, published between **1954** and **1955**, is the birth certificate of the . This subgenre of fantasy takes place in a completely imaginary world. The stakes are epic, between good and evil. **J.R.R. Tolkien**, born in **1892** and died in **1973**, created **Middle Earth**, a universe of unprecedented historical, linguistic and mythological depth. [[High Fantasy]]

The fruit of decades of work, this story meditates on power, ordinary heroism and loss. Tolkien does not just tell an adventure: he establishes a coherent world where each people has its own language, culture and history. Hobbits, elves, dwarves and men coexist there.

sections.title: Tolkien: the philologist creator of worlds

blocks.text: Tolkien was  professor at **Oxford**. [[Old English]] is the ancient form of English, spoken between the **Ve** and **XIth** centuries. His specialty, **philology**, studies languages ​​and their evolution. It is the basis of his universe. He first invented languages, Quenya and Sindarin, then imagined the people who spoke them.

blocks.caption: J.R.R. Tolkien, Oxford philologist who became father of modern fantasy.

blocks.text: By relying on the , he seeks to offer England its own mythology. Beowulf, the Nordic Edda and the Finnish Kalevala fuel his imagination. This process of  aims for a coherence so strong that the reader accepts the laws of this world as truths. The writer creates a secondary world with its own rules. [[Norse and Anglo-Saxon mythologies]] [[Tolkienian sub-creation]]
Tolkien rewrote the chapter "The Council of Elrond" over ten times to keep the family trees and linguistic nuances perfectly consistent.

sections.title: The quest for the Unique: an epic of fragility

blocks.text: The **One Ring**, forged by the fallen  **Sauron**, focuses its power. Sauron is a divine spirit of lower rank than the Valar, the “gods” of Tolkienian mythology. **Frodo Baggins**, a simple hobbit from the Shire, must destroy him at **Mount Destiny**, in the heart of **Mordor**, kingdom of shadow. blocks.text: The **Community of the Ring** brings together nine representatives of free peoples. While **Aragorn**, heir of , fights heroic battles, Frodo and **Sat** advance alone in solitude. [[Gondor]] is the main kingdom of Men in the south. The Ring gradually corrupts Frodo. Absolute power destroys even the most virtuous.

sections.title: Theology and philosophy: the refusal of allegory

blocks.text: Tolkien refuses explicit allegory, where each character represents a fixed idea. His work, however, explores **corruption by power**. The Ring attacks the will of its wearer. A hobbit without political ambition is the ideal candidate for this burden, because he has nothing to gain from power.

Past acts of mercy produce major consequences. **Gollum**, corrupted by the ring, is spared out of compassion on several occasions. Without knowing it, he allows the final accomplishment of the quest when Frodo, in turn, fails to throw the ring into the fire. Providence seems to work through pity, not force.

Published between **1954** and **1955**, the novel became one of the best-selling books of the 20th century. It sets the codes of modern fantasy: elves, dwarves, group quests, coherent secondary world. The film adaptation of **Peter Jackson**, from **2001** to **2003**, reinforces its global impact.

Tolkien also influences the role-playing game *Dungeons & Dragons*, music and ecology. His vision of nature threatened by technological excess still resonates today. The forges of Saruman and the machines of Sauron are the image of this. He has devoted more than half a century to Middle-earth.
Tolkien created languages ​​and a universe of absolute coherence of which **The Lord of the Rings** remains the undisputed masterpiece, founder of modern . [[High Fantasy]]
